name: Biochanin A

lead: Biochanin A is a phytoestrogen from red clover and other legumes, named as a component of Capixyl, a cosmetic peptide-and-isoflavone active for thinning scalp hair. People use it hoping for less thinning and fuller-looking hair.

The proposed route is scalp-level hormone-pathway effects. In lab assays it binds estrogen receptors and weakly inhibits an enzyme; trials of red clover isoflavones have addressed menopause and bone, and no hair study of the compound was found.

paras: It is used as a leave-on scalp serum or lotion as part of a regular routine, often alongside other thinning-hair products, with results judged over months.
As a phytoestrogen it has hormone-receptor activity in lab work. No safety data for topical hair use were found.

angle.text: Biochanin A is a red-clover phytoestrogen named in Capixyl, a cosmetic active for thinning hair. The idea is that it acts on scalp hormone pathways to slow thinning and keep hair looking fuller. It has been studied for menopause and bone, and hair studies were not found.

lead: Biochanin A is an O-methylated isoflavone, a plant phytoestrogen found in red clover, soy, alfalfa sprouts, peanuts and chickpea.[1] In hair-care marketing, red clover-derived biochanin A is named as a component of Capixyl, a cosmetic peptide-and-isoflavone hair-growth active.

The sources reviewed contain no clinical study of biochanin A for hair. Research on red clover isoflavones concerns other conditions, such as menopausal symptoms and osteopenia, and a 2025 review lists Capixyl among topical hair actives.[2]

paras: Wikipedia describes biochanin A as a phytoestrogen and a weak inhibitor of fatty acid amide hydrolase in vitro.[1] A 1998 study examined binding of phytoestrogens to estrogen receptor subtypes.[3] Isoflavone bioavailability in healthy women has been characterised for other isoflavones such as genistein and daidzein.[4]
No studies found on biochanin A for hair. Registered trials of red clover isoflavones address postmenopausal osteopenia, overactive bladder and menopausal symptoms rather than hair.[5][6][7]
